extracted.intended_audience: webmasters, digital publishers, researchers and general readers interested in web content and the attention economy
extracted.subtask_description: Explaining and identifying website content designed to hold users' attention and encourage repeat visits or longer time-on-site. Covers typical formats and the concept's relation to the attention economy and media manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: holding users' attention and encouraging return
rubrics_metrics.description: Sticky content is website content with the purpose of holding users' attention, so encouraging them to return to that particular website or to spend longer periods of time on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Webmasters use this method to build up a community of returning visitors to a website. (Article frames sticky content as a tactic within the attention economy.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Common formats/examples of sticky content
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples are chat rooms, online forums, webmail, Internet games, weather, news and horoscopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate typical implementations—interactive/community services, utility/frequent-update content, and entertainment—that tend to increase repeat visits and session length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to attention-economy and manipulation concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Sticky content is linked to related concepts such as the attention economy and clickbait, and sits among topics like infotainment, sensationalism, and news media manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or evaluating sticky content, consider ethical and editorial implications (e.g., potential for clickbait, sensationalism, bias, or manipulation) as raised by the article's related topics.
